biomarkers.name: KIT
biomarkers.clinical_use: KIT inhibitors such as imatinib in selected activating KIT alterations; nilotinib has also been studied

biomarkers.name: NRAS
biomarkers.clinical_use: No standard targeted therapy; MEK inhibitor trials

biomarkers.name: SF3B1
biomarkers.prevalence: ~10-20% overall; enriched in some anatomic sites

biomarkers.name: TMB
biomarkers.clinical_use: Generally lower immunotherapy responsiveness than cutaneous; combination nivolumab + ipilimumab often yields higher response than PD-1 monotherapy

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Atypical melanocytes at mucosal epithelium with invasive growth; often amelanotic
variants: by site: sinonasal, oral, oesophageal, anorectal, genitourinary
morphologic: lentiginous, nested, spindle cell, epithelioid, amelanotic
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Standard melanoma criteria (Breslow less applicable at mucosal sites)

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Often less inflamed than cutaneous melanoma, with lower TMB and generally lower response rates to immune checkpoint blockade

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Melanocytes at mucosal surfaces (sinonasal, oral, oesophageal, anorectal, genitourinary)
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Neural crest  melanocytes migrated to mucosal sites
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Melanocytic differentiation with variable pigmentation (often amelanotic); same lineage markers as cutaneous
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Same MITF-based cell state model but with distinct genomic biology  KIT and SF3B1 enriched, BRAF less common, low TMB (UV-independent); phenotype switching contributes to resistance
